SHANGHAI CHINA
MARCH 15, 1933
I have just come back to the Cathay Hotel from my second movie in three
and in spite of that disipation do not feel like going to bed, therefore will at least
make a start on a letter.
We, Pawley and Polin, went to see
"The Age of Consent" and
I cannot recommend it as a part of the entertainment program for a
convent. Maybe the
censors are not as active in China as the U.S. Anyway it was plenty rough. This is Wed-
nesday. On Monday we went to see John Barrymore in
" A Bill of Divorcement" which to my
is a great movie. Afterwards we went to a new Chinese dance hall which
has just been started. The building is a one story affair elaborately decorated in the
Skouras Bros. ) style - thoroughly American. The hall is about one
fifty feet square. There are no posts at all. Around the edge of the large
tables where you can sit and order drinks, the tables being arranged in
deep. A sign as you enter announces in several languages that men in
are not admitted. At one end an American jazz band of women musicians, music
lovers might object to
that description, who played all the very latest American jazz
music. Immediately around the hall seated on chairs there was a row of Chinese "host-
esses" who dance with the guests for ten cents Mex per dance. There were at least two
hundred Chinese and foreigners present. No one was drunk, in fact I have not yet seen
anyone full in China except some of our countrymen, and
those appeared to be on one of
the many cruises which put into Shanghai for one or two days. Many of the Chinese girls
of the hostess variety and also others who came with escorts, wear American clothes.
Most of them dance very well,
but the men aremostly in the beginner class. They are
awfully funny, perfectly dead in earnest, no exchange of small talk, no change in ex-
pression and apparently they are bored to death - except that they are very Scotch -
certainly would not be there if they were not getting what they consider their
moneys worth. I danced with two of the hostessess -
one at a time - and they were as
as either Gloria or Lucy Bixby
- I mean as dancers. They
tried to talk a few words
of some language possibly English but I couldn't make out what it was all about. Anyone
over here who is not Chinese is a
"foreigner", the Chinese not being able to tell an
American from an Englidhman, Frenchman or what have you. One girl who knew Mr. Polin
was named Mary MeTavish, her Father was and a Scotchman, as you might guess by her name,
and her Mother was Chinese. She
quite pretty and works as a stenographer for one of
Mr. Polin&s friends. These
Eurasians, as any offspring
of mixed races is called out
here, are to my way of thinking most
unfortunate. They are frequently disowned by both
races and are literally without
a country. Maj. Howard has a girl working in his office
whose Grandfather was English,
Grandmother Indian - thats too long a story to write out
the net of it is that she is a combination of English, Indian, Chinese, Japanese and
Italian and will probably marry
a Greek - so figure that out. The famous statement of
Bill Robertsons to Harry Guggenheim
that one nice thing about China was that "there were
no Jews over there"
is like most of
Bill's statements not entirely correct. Mr. Polin
is a perfect peach, but he should
eat ham. He introduced us to another Irishman by
the name of Ginsburg who
crowd of fellow Welshmen, Cohn,
Solomon and Strauss were
seated at a nearby table. We
lot of fun and I wish Bo and Frances could have seen
me stepping around with my accustomed grace with those Chinese girls. They wore
conventional Chinese dress with high collar which would make Queen Mary's costumes look
positively indecent. I felt like George Merck dancing with Jane Hotchkiss, or Theron
Catlin with Kitty Guy - take your pick.
Had tea Tuesday with Perry Hutton who called me up when he arrived here
with the ex-Marshal Chang Hsieu-liang. Perry is an old barn storming pilot who hails
from Wichita, Kansas, and used to be out at Lambert Field frequently. He came over here
originally with a trimotor Ford to demonstrate in Japan and China.
He sold the Ford to
the Young Marshalt, and stayed on as his personal pilot. The Marshal as you probably
have read has resigned as
the war lord of North China because he has been charged
the loss of Jehol, and now Perry will fly him on a pleasure trip to Europe, or
on. Hutton has been with the Marshal for three years and
great stories to tell about being shot at, trips where a forced landing would have
meant the massacre of the whole crowd, etc. He also told me some of
the inside story on
the operations in Jehol which were very interesting.
Must turn in now and get a little sleep. By the way have you heard how
the Charleston was invented? The inventor saw a Scotchman in front of a pay toilet,
Station HM B Shanghai signing off
